title: Fasting
definition: Fasting is the voluntary setting aside of food or another legitimate good for a time to seek God in prayer, humility, and dependence.
summary: Fasting is the voluntary setting aside of food or another legitimate good for a time to seek God in prayer, humility, and dependence.
christFocus: Jesus fasted, taught about fasting, and calls His people to seek the Father rather than perform spirituality for human approval.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Fasting is not a way to manipulate God. It is a physical expression of spiritual need, humility, and hunger for the Lord.

Scripture connects fasting with prayer, repentance, seeking guidance, grief, and dependence. It can help believers remember that they do not live by bread alone.

Christ-centered fasting looks to the Father, not to human recognition. The Holy Spirit uses fasting to expose desires and deepen dependence.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
In a world of constant appetite, fasting teaches believers that desire does not have to rule them. This can be especially meaningful for those learning Spirit-led self-control.

This doctrine also protects against performative religion. The point is not looking spiritual but seeking God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Fast with wisdom, humility, and prayer. Do not use fasting to punish yourself or impress others; use it to seek God, surrender desires, and rely more deeply on Christ.
